newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs, Jews hold separate marches for peace.
newsitem.headline: Arabs, Jews hold separate marches for peace.

text.p: Christian leaders on Sunday appealed to Israel to close a controversial tunnel in Jerusalem that triggered a wave of Israeli-Palestinian violence.
Church heads in Jerusalem held a joint mass at the Church of St Ann in Jerusalem's Old City before they led a peaceful march of about 2,000 Christian Arabs and foreigners towards the tunnel.

In West Jerusalem, about 10,000 Israeli peace activists marched from the grave of the late Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin to the home of his successor Benjamin Netanyahu demanding an end to violence and return to peace.

"For our Moslem brothers and sisters, the opening of the tunnel is a prelude to the opening of other tunnels which will inevitably lead to the compound of the (al-Aqsa) Mosque and the occupation of a part of it," a statement by the church heads read out during mass said.
"Therefore, what is required is the closure of the tunnel."
Israel has denied the tunnel harms Moslem holy places and there have been no reports of any Israeli plans to open new passageways.
Before the demonstration ended, Reverend Naim Atik of the Anglican church made a short prayer for peace.
"Almighty God, we lift our prayers to You. Our hearts are full of sadness for the dead and wounded. We cry to you for the sake of the Palestinian people."
Israeli police, on alert since the violence began on Wednesday, accompanied the demonstration that stretched for about one kilometer (half a mile), but did not intervene.
At the Israeli peace march, one woman said: "I am here today to demonstrate because I feel that the peace process is falling apart."

About 70 Palestinians and Israelis died in five days of confrontation across the West Bank and Gaza since the ancient passageway was opened near the Temple Mount, known to Moslems as Haram al-Sharif, site of Islam's third holiest shrine.
